W.—Clk., Zulu interp., and sub-distributor of stamps in the res. mag.'s office, Ixopo, Natal, 23rd Oct., 1876; dep. clk. of the peace for Ixopo, 2nd Mar., 1877; and on the 3rd Mar., 1879, apptd. in command of the Ixopo, Natal, native foot contingent, 800 strong; and subsequently transf'd. to command of the mounted contingent during the Zulu war; acted on several occasions as res. mag. of Ixopo; clk. to R.M., Weenen, July, 1886; admtr. of native law, Jagadi's location, 1889; mag., Lower Tugela div., 1894; R.M., Alfred div., 1895; mag., Lions River div., 1898; Umvoti div., 1904.

CROSSKILL, HERBERT.—Dep. prov. sec., Nova Scotia, 1868-78; again since 1882.

CROUCHER, F., M.B.—House surg., gen. Hosp., Singapore, 1893; col. surg., Malacca, Jan.,

CROWTHER, FRANCIS G.—Apptd. draughtsman, P.W.D., G. Coast, July, 1888; inspr. of schls., Aug., 1901; mem. bd. of ed., Jan., 1902; trav. comsnr., Apr., 1902; compiled statement of govt. lands, July to Sept., 1902; ag. dir. of educ. and sec. to bd. of educ., Nov., 1902, to Apr., 1903; trav. comsnr., Dec., 1903; ag. regis. of deaths, Apr., 1904; trav. comsnr., July, 1904; ag. dir. of educ., June, 1904.

CRUISE, H. R.—Ag. 4th clk., col. sec.'s off., Leeward Is., Feb. to May, 1904; ag. overseer of roads, May, 1904; ag. 3rd outdoor offr., treasy., May, 1904, to Feb., 1905; ag. 1st clk., P.O., Feb. to Apr., 1905; apptd. 4th indoor offr., treasy., Apr., 1905; atty.-gen.'s clk., Aug., 1905.

CUDDDEFORD, WM.—Employed on financial mission in Bahamas, May, 1885, to May, 1886; supervisor of customs, G. Coast, Jan., 1887; local auditor, Lagos, under C. and A.G., London, Dec., 1889; ditto, S. Leone and Gambia, Sept., 1893; auditor, Windward Is., May, 1896.

CUMBERLAND, CHAS. RUSSELL, B.A. OXON.—Entd. Ceylon civ. ser., 4th Oct., 1889; attached to the secretariat, 1st Apr., 1891; pol. mag., Balapitiya, 29th Sept., 1893; ditto, Panadure, 16th Dec., 1895; offr. of cls. IV., 15th May, 1898; dist. judge, Kegalla, 13th Dec., 1899; asst. govt. agt., Matale, 15th Aug., 1900; on special duty, camp for prisoners of war, Diyatalawa, 3rd Dec., 1900; offr. of cls. III., 9th June, 1901; 2nd asst. col. sec., 1st July, 1902; asst. govt. agt., Matale, 30th Oct., 1903; has held numerous ag. appts.

CUNLIFFE-OWEN, EDWARD, C.M.G. (1886).—B. 1847; for services in connection with the Col. and Ind. Exhibn., 1886.

CUNNINGHAM, J. FRANCIS, F.R.G.S., F.Z.S.—Ed. King's Coll., Lond., and part.; sec. to B.C. Africa adminstr., 24th Sept., 1892; orgnsd. printg. dept., and was apptd. editor of offl. gazette, June, 1894; served as vol. in campaigns against Zaraifi, etc., 1895 (recd. Central African medal); won gold medal offered by Zombie rifle club, 1897, and the Edwards Cup, 1898; ch. Br. comsnr. for delimitation of Anglo-Portuguese boundary in B.C. Africa, 24th May, 1899; priv. sec. to Sir H. Johnston's spec. miss. to Uganda, 24th Aug., 1899; passed exams. at Mid. Temp. and admitted a law student, 29th June, 1901; admitted to Gray's Inn, 1st July, 1901; sec. to Uganda adminstr., 1st Apr., 1901; apptd. judl. offr., 19th July, 1900; carried on duties of ch. judl. offr. and regis. in Uganda, 10th Apr., 1900, to 19th Dec., 1900; acted at headquarters for spec. comsnr. during his tour of inspection, 28th May to 8th June, 1900; and during the dep. comsnr.'s absence with Nandi expdtn., 9th Jan. to 16th Feb., 1901; present post, sec. to Uganda adminstr.; registr.-gen. of marriages, 1st Nov., 1902; joined Uganda vol. reserve, 1903; elected sec. of corps (company comdr.), 24th Jan., 1905; won annual championship and cup, 24th Mar., 1905; author of "Uganda and its Peoples," "Notes on the Anthropology and Ethnology of Indigenous Races," 1905.

CUNYNGHAME, SIR PERCY F., BART.—B. 1867; cadet, Sarawak civ. ser., July, 1886; asst. res. of Trusan, May, 1890; res. (2nd class), Mar., 1896; lieut. 3rd battn. Middlesex Rifles, May, 1897; capt., Oct., 190; ag. res., Limbang, May, 1899; res., 2nd class, Upper Rejang, Aug., 1901; commdt., Sarawak Rangers, July, 1903; res., 1st div., and mem. of sup. coun., May, 1904.

CURLEWIS, JOHN STEPHEN, B.A., LL.B. (Cape).—Cape civ. serv., 1883-1888; advocate, sup. ct., Cape Colony, 12th Oct., 1887; advocate,
high ct. (late S.A.R.), May, 1888; counsel for Imperial govt. in arbitn. with late S.A.R. re Asiatic question, 1895; ag. judge of high ct. (late S.A.R.), 15th Apr., 1899, to 31st Jan., 1901; pres. of crim. ct. for Witwatersrand, 2nd Nov., 1899, to 31st Jan., 1900; puisne judge, sup. ct., Transvaal, 1st Sept., 1903.

CURLING, C. NAPIER.—Apptd. res. just. and collr. of Elenthua, Bahamas, Aug., 1895; ch. registr., G. Coast, 12th Jan., 1899; dist. consmr., Mar., 1899; ch. registr. and sheriff, 1901.

CURMI, TANCRED.—Asst. supt. of pol., Malta, 1890; senr. asst., 1902; supt., 1903.

CURRIE, SIR DONALD, G.C.M.G. (1897), K.C.M.G. (1881), C.M.G. (1877).—B. 1825; chmn. of the Union-Castle Mail Packets Co. In July, 1876, at the time of the negotiations between the Earl of Carnarvon and Pres. Brand, he assisted by his good offices in bringing about the success of these negotiations, and thus ending the long dispute between the Br. Govt. and the Orange Free State in reference to the diamond fields; formerly M.P. for Perthshire.

CUSACK-SMITH, SIR BERRY, K.C.M.G. (1898).—B. 1859; ed. at Eton; barrister, Middle Temp., 1884; law scholarship, 1883; formerly lieut. 1st V.B. Essex regt.; apptd. H.M. Consul at Samoa, Jan., 1890, and H.M. dep. consmr. for the W. Pacific at Samoa, May, 1890; proceeded in H.M.S. "Curacoa" to Union Group to report on land claims, Aug., 1892; dep. consmr. for the Samoan and Union Groups, and authorised to perform the duties of res. in the Union Group, Oct., 1892; special judicial consmr., Apr., 1893; apptd. to license and superintend employment of Gilbert Is. natives in Samoa, Jan., 1894; consul-gen., Valparaiso, 1897.

CUSCADEN, W. A.—Sen. Sophister, Trin. Coll., Dub.; capt. 4th Roy. Dub. Fus.; asst. inspr. of constab., G. Coast, 1879; civil consmr., Tacquah, 1881; ch. inspr. of pol., Singapore, 1883; asst. supt. of pol., Penang, 1884; ag. pol. supt., Malacca, 1889, and July, 1897; Singapore, 1891, and Apr., 1893; asst. supt. of pol., P.W., 1893; supt. pol., Malacca, July, 1897; ag. supt. pol., Singapore, Apr., 1898; ag. inspr. gen. pol. S.S. Mar., 1901, to Aug., 1902, and Nov., 1903, to Mar., 1904; supt. of pol., Sing., Aug., 1902.

CUTHBERT, SIR HENRY, M.L.C., K.C.M.G. (1897).—B. 1829; min. of justice, Victoria, 1886-90; solr.-gen., 1894.

DA'ETT, JOHN.—Ed. at King's Coll., Lond.; asst. draughtsman, P.W.D., Jamaica, Jan., 1873; ch. ditto, Mar., 1875; dist. engnr., N. (now W.) Dist., Jan., 1883; engnr., Kingston Dist., 1886; asst. dir. pub. wks., Jamaica, 10th Mar., 1902.

DALE, CHARLES ERNEST.—Ed. at Greenwich and King's Coll., London; fell. soc. accnts. and auditors, fell. roy. statistical soc.; apptd. dir. customs Niger Coast Protec., Jan., 1895; asst. postmr.-gen., Apr., 1896; ag. dir.-gen. customs and postmr.-gen., Feb. to Sept., 1896, Oct., 1897, to June, 1898, Oct., 1899, to Feb., 1901; Dec., 1900, to July, 1901; treasr. Southern Nigeria, Feb., 1898; ag. sec., Feb. to April, 1900; Jan. to Apr., 1903, dir. pub. officers' guarantee fund, Apr., 1900; ag. treas., Lagos, Sept., 1904.

DALE, H. E.—Ed. at St. Paul's Schl. and at Oxford; class. schol., Balliol Coll., 1894; Hartford school, 1895; Craven schol., 1895; Ireland schol., 1896; 1st class mods., 1896; 1st class lit. hum., 1898; B.A., 1898; Fell. New Coll., 1898; Derby schol., 1899; M.A., 1901; apptd., after compet. exam., 2nd class clk., C.O., Oct., 1898; sent on special mission to Br. Hond., Nov., 1903.

DALE, HAROLD ROSS.—Entered atty.-gen.'s office, Cape, Dec., 1879; 2nd class clk., July, 1883; ch. clk. to solr.-gen., Grahamstown, Mar., 1885; ch. clk. to atty.-gen., Nov., 1886; J.P. for dist. of Albany; reger. of sup. ct. and taxing offr., 1st June, 1901.

DALLAS, FRANCIS HENRY.—Ed. Univ. Coll. School; asst. sec. Penang municipality, 1895; ag. sec. May, 1896; Sarawak civ. sec.; ag. editor "Sarawak Gazette," and manager, Sarawak gov't. printing office, 1897; ag. treas. and clk., supreme coun., June, 1902; treas. and recorder of sup. coun., 1903; mem. of comte. of adminstr., 1903-4.

DALTON, THE REV. CANON JOHN NEALE, M.A., C.M.G. (1882).—B. 1839; was gov. to T.R.H. Princes Albert Victor and George of Wales, and ag. chaplain to H.M.S. "Bacchante"; chaplain in ord. to Her Majesty, 1886; canon of Windsor, 1885.

DALY, SIR MALACHY BOWES, K.C.M.G. (1900).—B. 1836; Lieut.-Governor of Nova Scotia, 1890.

DALY, THE HON. THOMAS MAYNE, K.C.—Mem. for Selkirk, Manitoba, in Dominion house of commons; min. of interior, Canada, 1892-4.

DANAVALL, JOHN MARTIN.—Barrister, Mid. Temp., 1877; ag. solr.-gen., Leeward Is., 1883; again in 1884; ag. mag. Dist. C, 1883, and again in 1885; 2nd puisne judge, Leeward Is., June, 1888; also dep.-judge of the vice-admiralty et al., 1889.

DANDY, JOSEPH HENRY.—Ed. Oakes Inst., Liverpool, certif. as inspr. of nuisances and sanitary inspr. from sanitary inst., 1896; 1st cl. advanced hygiene, S. Kensington, 1897; surveying (1st cl.) and certif. of sanitary knowledge, Victoria Univ., 1898; certif. schl. of hygiene, Univ. Coll., 1898; practical bacteriology, Univ. Coll., 1899; mem. of san. inst., 1900; san. inspr., Liverpool, chief sanitary inspr., Hong Kong, June, 1899.

DANE, ROBT., M.R.L.S., L.S.A. (1887), L.R.C.P. (1889).—House physician, Middlesex hosp., 1890; house surg., gen. hosp., Singapore, June, 1890; col. surg., Prov. Wellesley, Mar., 1893; col. surg., Sing., March, 1901; ag. col. surg. res., Sing., May, 1905; mem. of S. S. med. coun., July, 1905.

DANIEL, ROWLAND MORTIMER.—Ed. at St. Edmund's, Canterbury; 2nd Lieut., Glam. artil. militia, 1893; certif. of musk., Hythe; capt. and instr. of gunnery, 1898; seconded sub.-inspr., B.S.A. pol., Div. I. (now Bech. Prot. pol.), 1898; served through S. African war, 1900-02, including siege of Mafeking; ment. in desps.; brig. sig. offr. and staff capt., 1900-01; ag. asst. consmr., S. Bech. Prot., 1902; asst. res. mag. at Serowe, 1903; ag. asst. consmr., N. Prot., 1904.

DANIELL, HUMPHREY A.—Ed. at Eton; served with Hampshire regt. in S. Africa, 1901-02 (medal and 5 clasps); asst. dist. offr., Somaliland, Feb., 1906.

DANSEY, CLAUDE EDWARD MARJORIBANKS.—Ed. at Wellington; lieut., Lancas. Fusiliers; served during Matabeleland rebellion, 1896, with Matabele mounted pol. (medal); sub. comlt., B. N. Borneo constab., during operations against rebels under Mohamed Salleh, May, 1899, to Jan., 1900 (medal); commanded squadron 1st African Light Horse during South African War, 1900-2 (2 medals and 6 clasps); staff-lieut. for intell. and A.D.C. to G.O.C., Harrismith dist., S. Africa, 1902-4; specially mentd. by gov. of B. N. Borneo for services during expdh. in interior, and mentd. in desp., S. Africa, 1900; asst. dist. offr., Somaliland, 4th Nov., 1901.
DARLEY, Cecil W., I.S.O. (1903).—Engnr.-in-ch. for harbours and river navig. and water supply, N. S. Wales, 1891.

DARLEY, Sir Fred., Matthew, P.C. (1905), G.C.M.G. (1901), K.C.M.G. (1897), K.T. Bach. (1887).—B. 1830; Ed. Dungannon Coll. and Trinity Coll., Dublin; B.A., Hon. LL.D., T.C., 1903; barrister, Ireland, 1853, N. S. Wales, 1862, Queensland, 1886; Q.C., 1878; M.L.C., N. S. Wales, 1868-1886; vice-pres., exec. coun., N. S. Wales, 1881-2-3; ch. just., N. S. Wales, 1886; lieut.-gov., N. S. Wales, 1891; acted as such six times for periods amounting in all to nearly 3 years, besides frequently as deputy for different governors; apptd. one of the comsrs. to inquire into South African War, 1902.

DARNLEY, E. R.—Scholar of Trin. Coll., Camb., 1893; of Lond. Univ., 1897; B.A. (sixth wrangler) and B.Sc., 1897; apptd., after compet. exam., 2nd class elk., C.O., 11th Oct., 1898.

DARTNELL, Major-Gen. Sir J. G., K.C.B. (1901), C.M.G. (1881).—B. 1838; late of the 27th and 86th regts.; comdt. of the volr. and mounted pol., Natal, 1874; ret., 1903.

DASHWOOD, Chas. James.—Govt. res. and judge of the N. territory of S. Australia, 1892-1895; mem. H. of Assem., S. Australia, 1887-92; crown solr., 1905.

DAVIDSON, Andrew, M.D., F.R.C.P. Edin.; M.R.C.S. Eng.; Fellow Royal Physical Soc.—Formerly physician to the ct. of Madagascar, visiting and suptndg. surg. civil hosp., Mauritius, Feb., 1877, and govt. analyst, Dec., 1877; acted as pol. and prison surg. in 1878; prof. of chem., Roy. Coll., Apr., 1879; supt. lun. asyl., Nov., 1879; author of numerous med. wks.; sec. to cattle plague comsn., etc.; medical adviser of the C.O., Edinburgh, 1897.

DAVIDSON, Walter Edward, C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1859; scholar and exhibitor of Christ's Coll., Camb.; writer, Ceylon civ. ser., Aug., 1880; attached to Kandy Kachcheri, Dec., 1880; writer col. sec.'s office, Apr., 1881; transferred to Colombo Kachcheri, Sept., 1881; attached to the Negombo pol. ct., May, 1882; acted as asst. agt., Negombo, July to Oct., 1882; extra office asst., Colombo Kachcheri, May, 1883; and ag. office asst., Nov., 1884; sec. to Colon comsn., col. exhib., 1886; ag. asst. gov't. agt., Kegalla, Apl., 1888, Mar., 1892, and Feb., 1895; ag. pol. mag., Kalutara, Apl., 1899; Galle, Dec., 1890; pol. mag., Matale, Feb., 1887; Haldummulla, Oct., 1890; ag. dist. judge, Kalutara, Apl., 1899; ag. gov't. agt. and fiscal, prov. of Sabaragamuwa, July, 1896; asst. gov't. agt., Kegalla, Oct., 1896; N. Eliya, Feb., 1899; chmn. mun. coun., and mayor of Colombo, Apl., 1898; resig. as chmn. of mun. coun., going on leave; asst. sec. to administrator, Transvaal, 1901; col. sec., 1902-3; gov., Seychelles, 15th Apr., 1904.

DAVIDSON-HOUSTON, Lieut.-Col., Wilfred B.—Ed. at Corrig schl., Ireland, and St. Edward's, Oxford; 2nd lieut. 5th Royal Dublin Fus., Jan., 1887; capt., 1892; major, 1902; lieut.-col., 1906; B.S.A. Co. pol., and asst. comsnr., Rhodesia, 1890-92; certificates, R.I.C. and Dublin met. pol., 1895; asst. inspr., G. Coast Contab. (Hausas), Jan., 1894; inspr., Jan., 1898; capt., W. A. F. F., Jan., 1898; on spec. serv. Kwahu and Ashanti-Akim, Feb., 1894, to Mar., 1895; Ashanti expedn., 1895-6, commanded advance guard, main column (hon. ment. in desp., star); spec. miss. to N.W. Ashanti, Feb. to May, 1896; with Hausa detach. in London, Jubilee, 1897 (medal); operations in N. T., G. Coast, 1897-8 (medal and clasp); ag. res., Ashanti, May, 1899, to Apr., 1900; Ashanti campaign, 1900 (medal and clasp); S. African War, 1901-2, staff offr., Warrenton (medal and 5 clasps); adjutant 5th Roy. Dub. Fus., 1902; comsnr. of Ashanti, 1902; ag. ch. comsnr. of Ashanti, Mar. to May, 1903; and from July, 1904, to Mar., 1905; comsnr. of Montserrat, 25th Apr., 1906.

DAVIES, C. Rees.—Ed. at Eton; admitted solr. of sup. ct., Sept., 1891; under-sheriff, Pembrokeshire, 1897; called to the bar, Bahamas, July, 1901; ag. ch. just., Feb., 1903; ag. prosecuting coun. for the Crown, May, 1903; coroner, Nov., 1904; registr.-gen., Br. Hond., Apr., 1905; also registr., Vice-Admiralty ct.; ag. atty.-gen., June, 1905, to Jan., 1906, and mem. of ex. and leg. couns.; also mem. of bds. of educn. and quarantine; J.P. for col.; ag. atty.-gen., May, 1906.

DAVIES, Hon. John Mark.—M.L.C. for S. Yarra, Victoria, 1889; for Melbourne, 1894; min. for just., 1890-92; solr.-gen., 1893-1900, and 1902-3; min. of pub. instrn., 1903; atty.-gen. and solr.-gen., Victoria, 1903.

DAVIES, Hon. Sir Louis Henry, K.C.M.G. (1897).—B. 1845; called to the bar, 1866; Q.C. in 1880; was one of the Canadian counsel before the internat. fishery comsn. at Halifax in 1877; solr. gen. of P.E. Is., 1869, and again in 1872-3; led the opposition in P.E. Is. Legislature until Sept., 1876, when he became premier and atty.-gen.; resig. in Mar., 1879, and was defeated at the gen. elections which followed; was first returned to the House of Commons at the gen. elections in 1882, and has since sat for Queen's; min. of marine and fisheries in Sir W. Laurier's govt., June, 1896; mem. joint high comsn., Quebec and Washington, 1898-9; puisne judge of sup. court, 1901.

DAVIES, The Hon. Sir Matthew Henry, K.T. Bach. (1890).—B. 1851; solr.; late mayor of Prahran; mem. exec. coun. Victoria; min. without portfolio, Feb., 1886; speaker, legis. assem., 1887-92; vice-pres. and an exec. comsnr. for the centennial internat. exhibn., 1888.

DAVIES, Wm. Rees.—Ed. Eton and Trin. Hall, Camb.; B.A., 1885; called to bar (Inner Tem.), 1887; went South Wales circuit; J.P. and dep. lieut. Pembrokehire; M.P. for Pemb., 1892-3; asst. priv. sec. to chancellor of exchequer, 1893-5; atty.-gen., Bahamas, Dec., 1897; administered the govt., June, 1901; ag. ch. just., May to Aug., 1902; King's advocate, Cyprus, 1902.

DAVIS, Beccles.—Ed. C.M.S. grammar schl., Sierra Leone and Fourah Bay Coll. (Dunelm); 1st class customs officer, 1894; ag. statistical officer of customs, Niger Coast Prot., Apr. to Oct., 1894; P.C.O. at Opobo, Brass and Bonny, 1894 to 1899; supervisor of customs, Southern Nigeria, 1900; transferred to pub. wks. dep., 1903; accent., P.W.D., 1903.

DAVIS, C. G. H.—Ent. col. ser. of Br. Guiana as asst. clk. audit office, Nov., 1887; 5th cl. clk., Apr., 1889; 4th Sept., 1889; 3rd Jan., 1894; sec. to comtee. of combined court on exp. expenditure, 1893-4; 2nd cl. clk., Nov., 1896; ag. 1st cl. clk., 1895-6-7-8; ag. acct. to sup. ct., July, 1899, to Sept., 1900; 1st clk. and accent., post office, Sept., 1900.

DAVIS, C. T.—Ed. Christ's Coll., Brecon, and Oxford; classical scholar, Balliol coll., 1892-6; 1st class classical mods., 1894; Jenkyns exhib., 1896; 1st class lit. hum., 1896; appld. after compet. exam., 1st cl. clk., acct-gen.'s dept.,
admiralty, Oct. 5th, 1896; transfd. to sec.'s dept., inland rev., Mar., 1897; 2nd cl. clk., col. office, Apr. 15th, 1897; went to Gibraltar as sec. to Rt. Hon. Sir C. R. Thompson on a mission to inquire into the currency question, May and June, 1898; sec. Pacif. cable comtee., 1900; priv. sec., to Sir M. Ommannay, June, 1902; 1st cls. clk., 1st Apr., 1905.

DAVIS, L. A. R.—Permanent supernum. aid waiter, cust. dept., B. Guiana, Oct., 1882; 6th cl., Apr., 1883; 4th cl., Oct., 1884; 4th cl. offr. of cust., Jan., 1886; 3rd cl., Oct., 1887; 2nd cl., June, 1896; ag. 1st grade comsry. of taxation and offl. astt. to comptlr. of cust. in excise matters, July, 1898, to Mar., 1899; 1st cl. offr., 8th Sept., 1905; ag. survr. of cust., 1st Nov., 1905, to 28th Feb., 1906.

DAVIS, NICHOLAS DARNELL, C.M.G. (1895).—B. 1846; was for some years in Grenada, in the priv. sec.'s office; priv. sec. to Admstr. Baynes for a short time, In Br. Guiana served as clerk in several depts.; Aug., 1870, to Feb., 1871, sec. to the comsrs. of inquiry into the treatment of imgrts.; sec. to roy. comsrs. of inquiry into the treatment of imgrts. in Mauritius, Feb., 1872; comdt., Br. Sherbro, S. Leone, 1874; postmr.-gen., Br. Guiana, 1876; acted as rec-gen., Dec., 1880, to Sept., 1881; comptroller of customs, 1st Oct., 1881; ag. auditor-gen., mem. of the ct. of policy, and sen. comsrr. of the Vissengen estate, 1882; mem. ct. of policy again in 1886; auditor gen., 1st July, 1898; mem. exec. coun., Br. G., Feb., 1901; has acted as gov. sec. on eight occasions, and three times as dep. govr.

DAVIS, S. SPENCER.—Extra rev. offr., St. Kitts, 1893; 4th ditto, 1895; asst. treas., Gold Coast, 1901.

DAVSON, CHARLES SIMON, B.A., LL.D., K.C.—Ed. at Westminster and Trin. Hall, Camb.; called to the bar, Middle Tem., Jan., 1881; admitted to bar of Br. Guiana, 1882; acted as solr.-gen. on many occasions; stip. mag., 1888; solr.-gen., 1898; ag. atty.-gen., Nov., 1898, to Oct., 1899; again, Oct., 1900, to Apr., 1901; puisne judge, Mauritius, 1905.

DAWE, HON. CHAR.—Newfoundland: M.H.A., Harbour Grace, 1878-1889; for Port-de-Grave since 1898; mem. exec. coun. (without portfolio), 1894, and again in 1897.

DAWE, HON. E.—M.H.A. for Harbour Grace, Newfoundland, 1889-1905; rlwy. comsrr., 1890; financial sec., 1893; chrmn., bd. of wks., 1895; min. of agric. and mines, 1900; mem. of cabinet, 1903; min. of marine and fisheries, 1904.

DAWSON, J. B. H.—M.R.C.S. Eng., L.R.C.P. Lond., 1893, St. Mary's Hosp. med. schl., Lond.; dist. med. offr., Leeward Isl., Oct., 1894; dist. surg. of Sierra Leone Aug., 1893.

DAWSON, JOHN WILDING.—Asst. eng., drainage dept., Mauritius, 30th Nov., 1894; drainage authority, 15th August, 1898; asst. dir. of pub. wks. and surveys, 28th Dec., 1904.

DAWSON, SAMUEL EDWARD, C.M.G. (1906).—Queen's printer, Canada, and controller of stationery, Nov., 1891; doc. of letters, Leval. Univ., Quebec, and fell. of roy. soc. of Canada.

DAY, H. R. A.—Cadet, Sarawak civ. service, July, 1886; asst. res. Lundu, June, 1881; asst. res. Bitulu, June, 1893; res. 2nd cl., Mar., 1896; res. of Lundu, 1898; res., 2nd cl., Upper Sarawak, Jan., 1902.

DEACON, THOMAS.—Apptd., after open compet. exam., for the home civ. ser., to the Impl. Post Office, July, 1884; postmr.-gen., Gold Coast Colony, Sept. 2nd, 1899; lieut., G. C. Rifle vols., 1899; capt., 13th Oct., 1901; ag. adjutant, 11th Apr., 1903.

DEAKIN, THE HON. ALFRED.—Comsrr. of pub. wks. and min. of water supply, Victoria, Mar. 8th, 1883; and also vice-pres. bd. of land and works; solr.-gen. Nov. 13th, 1883; pres. of roy. coms. on water supply, Dec., 1884; ch. sec. and min. of water supply, 1886; resig., Nov., 1890; sen. deleg. to col. confce., 1887; one of the Austr. delegates sent to Eng. in connection with Austr. federation bill; joined 1st ministry of the Commonwealth as atty.-gen. and min. of justice, Jan., 1901; prime min. of Australia, 1903-4, again prime min., 1905.

DEALY, THOMAS KIRKMAN, F.R.G.S., M.R. San. I.—Ed. at St. Mary's Coll., Hammersmith; Marquis of Ripon's 1st prize and a double first (head of each list), 1880; matric. (1st div.), Lond. Univ., 1883; 1st B.A. (1st div.), 1884; Diplôme (degré supérieur) de l'Alliance Française (Paris), 1902; J.P., 1904; headmr. St. Mary's Derby, 1881-84; asst. master, govt. central schl., now Queen's Coll., Hong Kong, 1884; hon. examr. in physics to coll. of medicine for Chinese, 1888; passed 2nd standard higher grade Chinese, Aug., 1890; ag. 2nd master, Victoria Coll., Apr., 1890, to Sept., 1891, Apr., 1894, to Apr., 1895, Mar., 1899, to Apr., 1900, May, 1900, to Oct., 1901, and Mar. to Sept., 1904; apptd. master in charge, pol. schl., Sept. 1st, 1900; resig. pol. schl., 30th Apr., 1906; apptd. 2nd mast., Queen's Coll., 16th Mar., 1906.

DE BOISSIERE, ARNAULD.—Entd. civ. serv., Trinidad, 1891; trooper, light horse, 1897; sub-lieut., 1901; lieut., 1903; ag. chief of fire brigade, Mar., 1903; J.P. for colony, and inspr. of Indian immgrts.

DE CELLES, ALFRED DUCLOS.—Joint librarian of parlmt., Canada, 1885.

DE FREITAS, ANTHONY, B.A. (Cantab.).—Called to the bar, Lincoln's Inn; ag. pol. mag. and coroner for E. dist., Grenada, 1900 and 1901; ag. atty.-gen., St. Vincent, Nov., 1902; ag. pol. mag. and coroner, S. dist., Grenada, Nov., 1902; ag. regis., sup. ct., Grenada, Dec., 1902, to Jan., 1904; ag. pol. mag. and coroner, S. dist., Grenada, July, 1903; ag. ch. just., mem. ex. and leg. couns., and mem. bd. of educ., St. Vincent, May to Oct., 1904; pol. mag. and coroner, 1st dist., St. Lucia, Oct., 1904.

DE GRUCHY, A. NICOLLE, M.B., C.M., Edin.—Asst. med. offr., and J.P., Victoria, Seychelles, and outlying islands, 11th Sept., 1901; col.-surg., S. Nigeria, Apr., 1906.

DE KRETZER, EDWARD, I.S.O. (19·3).—B. 1854; employed in col. sec.'s off., Ceylon, 8th May, 1872; asst. aud.-gen., 1st Jan., 1901.

DE LA CORNILLIERE, HENRI GASTON ERNEST.—Draughtsman, P.W.D. of late O.F.S., Nov., 1892, to Mar., 1900; architectural asst., P.W.D., O.R.C., Mar., 1900, to July, 1902; head of architectural drawing off., ditto, July, 1902.

DELAFAYE, SIR LOUIS VICTOR, KT. BACH. (1898)—B. 1842; called to bar Mid. Tem., 1863; mun. councillor, St. Louis, 1870; prov. judge, sup. ct., Mauritius, Mar., 1879; mem. prison bd., Jan., 1884; mem. civ. ser. inquiry comsnn., Feb., 1884; mem. civ. ser. comsnn., 1884-95; ag. puisne judge, 1884-5, and May, 1890, to July, 1892; Q.C., Aug., 1892; puisne judge, Nov., 1894; ag. chief justice, June, 1898; chief judge, Dec., 1898.

DELFOSSÉ, LOUIS EDWARD.—Clk. in H.M.'s naval dockyard from Aug., 1869, to Aug., 1871; 3rd cl. clk. in the med. office, Aug., 1871; 1st cl.
DE SARAM, J.H., C.M.G. (1901).—B. 1844; writer to the govt. of Ceylon, 1865; pol. mag. of Balapiti-módara, 1866; dist. judge, Badulla, Oct., 1867; comsnr. of requests, Colombo, 1868; dist. judge, Kurunégala, 1875; regis.-gen., Colombo, 1886; dist. judge, Kalutara, Dec., 1883; registr.-gen., May, 1886; dist. judge, Jaffna, Aug., 1891; ditto, Galle, Dec., 1891; ditto, Kandy, Aug., 1893; ret.

DESCROIZILLES, FREDERIC VIVIAN.—Ed. Royal coll., Mauritius; inspr. of distill., Mauritius, May, 1874; asst. recvr.-gen., 16th June, 1897.

DESHON, EDWARD, C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1836; mem. of land bd., Queensland; ensign in 68th L.I., June, 1854; lieut., Dec., 1854; served with 68th L.I. at siege and fall of Sebastopol, from Nov., 1854, to end of the war; medal and clasp, and Turkish medal; instructor of musketry to the 68th L.I. from Nov., 1857, to Oct., 1861; passed compet. exam. for admission to Staff Coll., in July, 1861; ret. by sale of comsn. in Oct., 1861; audit.-gen., Queensland, 1890; ret. 1901.

DES MARAIS, HENRY EUGENE.—Called to the bar, Mid. Tem., Apr., 1866; pol. mag., Rodrigues, June, 1875; dist. judge and stip. mag., Seychelles, Nov., 1879; ag. ch. civ. comsnr. on several occasions; ag. mag., Moka, Apr. to Sept., 1882; dist. mag., Moka, Aug., 1884; ag. pol. and additional mag., Port Louis, Nov., 1884; dist. mag., Moka, Dec., 1885; ag. jun. dist. mag., Port Louis, May to October, 1886; Mar., 1887, to Jan., 1888; dist. and stip. mag., Moka, July, 1889.

DE SMIDT, HENRY, C.M.G. (1901), B.A. (Cape Univ.), F.S.S.—B. 1845; entered the service in Mar., 1865; permanent under col. sec. of the col. of Cape of Good Hope, and perm. head of convicts and prisons dept., holding in addition the following offices: (1) accounting offrr., col. sec.'s dept.; (2) controller printg. and statnry.; (3) mem. civ. ser. comsn.; (4) mem. tender bd.; (5) custodian stamps; (6) admstr. food and drugs act; (7) inspr. emigrt. coolie ships. Was specially charged with the duties of dir. of the census of 1891; received congratulations of the govt., and was awarded an honorarium of 500L specially voted by parlmt.; elected fellow of roy. statistical soc., 1892; asst. treas., July, 1898; ret. 1904.

DES VŒUX, SIR GEORGE W., G.C.M.G. (1893), K.C.M.G. (1883), C.M.G. (1877).—B. 1834; ed. Charterhouse, and Balliol Coll., Oxon. Called to the bar of Upper Canada, 1861; stip. mag., Br. Guiana, 1863; admstr. of the govt., St. Lucia, 1869; ag. gov. of Trinidad, Jan., 1877, to Jan. 1878; ag. gov. of Fiji, June, 1878, to Sept., 1879; gov. Bahamas, 1880; gov., Fiji, 1880-6; asst. high comsnr. W. Pacific, 1880, and high comsnr., 1882-5; gov. of Newfoundland, 1886; of Hong Kong, 1887; ret. 1891.

DEVILLIERS, RT. HON. SIR JOHN, P.C. (1897), K.C.M.G. (1882), KT. BACH. (1877).—B. 1842; ch. justice of the sup. ct., C. of Good Hope, 1874; atty-gen., from 1872 to 1874; for several years mem. of the legis. assem.; pres. of the legis. coun., and mem. of the coun. of the Univ. of C. of Good Hope in 1873; one of the roy. comsn. for the settlement of the affairs of the Transvaal, 1881; represented the Cape at the col. confece., Ottawa, 1894; mem. of judicial comte., H.M. privy coun., 1897.

DEW, ARTHUR TOMKYNES.—Naval cadet, 1867; midshipman, 1869; sub.-lieut., 1874; took part in the expdns. to the Linggi and Lukut rivers in 1874, and in suppression of piracy on Malayan coast (Indian medal, with Perak clasp); mag. and collr., Perak, 1881; sup. Br. territory of Dindings, 1884; dep. master attendant, shipping master,
Singapore, 1886; is a J.P.; mag., Singapore and Penang; comsnr. ct. of requests; mag. and collr., dist. mag. and harbrmr., Matang, Perak, 1888; dist. mag., Krian, Apr., 1899; ag. dist. mag., Lower Perak, July, 1901; dist. offr., Batang Padang, Perak, Nov., 1902; dist. offr., Lower Perak, 14th Sept., 1904.

DEWAR, H. J.—Apptd. clk., repatriation, O.R.C., 23rd April, 1902; ditto, British refugee aid, 1st July, 1903; ditto, treasy., 1st July, 1903; examr. of acts., treasy., 4th Apr., 1906.

DEWDNEY, THE HON. EDGAR.—Lieut.-gov. of N.W. territories, 1881; min. of interior, Canada, 1888; lieut.-gov., Br. Columbia, 1892-7.

DE WET, THE HON. SIR JACOBUS ALBERTUS, K.C.M.G. (1890).—B. 1840; mem. Cape house of assem. and exec. coun.; min. for native affairs, 1884; Br. agent, S.A. Republic, June, 1890; ret. on pension, Sept., 1890.

DE WILTON, MAJOR ALBERT WALTER.—lieut., Lanarkshire militia, 1881; lieut., Connaught Rangers, 1883 to 1886; lieut., Indian staff corps, 1886 to 1894; capt., ditto, 10th Mar., 1894; major, ditto, 10th July, 1891; served in Burma campaign, 1885, 1887, 1889 (medal and two clasps); insp.-gen. of police, Mauritius, 29th Oct., 1898; insp.-gen. of pol. and prisons, Ceylon, 18th Aug., 1902.

DE WOLF, A.—Med. visitor of estates, Trinidad, 1st Apr., 1874; dist. med. offr., St. Joseph, 1st Jan., 1876; ditto, Port of Spain North, med. insp. of imigrts., and health offr. of shipping, Aug., 1890; ag. surg.-gen., on several occasions, 1884-1899; surg.-gen., 5th Nov., 1901.

DEWS, ALBERT, M.A.—Classical master, Codrington Coll., Barbados, 1893.

DIAS, FELIX REGINALD, M.A., LL.M. Trin. Hall, Camb.—Called to the bar, Inner Tem., May, 1887; pol. mag. and comsnr. of requests, Gampola, Ceylon, Oct., 1889; crown counsel for the island, July, 1893.

DICK, JOHN NORMAN.—Govt. engrnr. survr., Penang, 1888; ag. govt. marine survr., Singapore, June, 1895 to June, 1896; govt. mar. surv., Singapore, March, 1901.

DICKSON, THOMAS.—Ed. at Fettes Coll., Edin.; served in Boer war in Ist. cont., Ceylon M.I., Jan., 1900, to Jan., 1901 (medal and 3 clasps); and in S.A.C. from Jan., 1901, to June, 1902 (King's medal and 2 clasps); temp. apptd. ch. clk., land settm. dept., O.R.C., 10th Oct., 1901; asst. sec., land settm., 12th Aug., 1903; sec., land settm., 23rd Jan., 1905; ag. dir., land settm., 14th May to 14th Nov., 1906.

DILLON, A. BARROW.—Ed. Queen's Roy. Coll., Trinidad; clk. to insp. of schls., B. Hond., 1893; ag. clk. to auditor and in treasy. and customs, 1893; clk. to col. engrnr., 1895; ag. insp. of schls., 1895-8; 2nd clk., treasy. and cust., 1897; insp. of schls., June, 1898; ag. supt. bot. station, 28th Sept. to 31st Dec., 1904; ag. ch. clk., C.S.O., and clk. of couns., 29th June, 1905.

DILLON, P. L., I.S.O. (1904).—B. 1846; 4th class landing waiter, Barbados, 1866; 3rd class, 1868; senior, 1880; landing survr., 1886; comptr. of customs, Dec., 1890.

DISCOMBE, JOHN.—Apptd., after compet. exam., 3rd class clk., sup. ct., Gibraltar; 2nd class clk. (supernumerary), Jan., 1890; ag. asst. registr., Nov., 1899; asst. registr. and dep. clk. of arraigns, Jan., 1900; ag. registr. and adminstr.-gen., July to Sept., 1901.

DOBIE, EDWARD DAVID.—Crown solr., Tasmania (also clk. of the peace and registr. of building socs.), May, 1887; barrister, etc., sup. ct., Tasmania, admitted July, 1882; joined civ. ser., Tasmania, Mar., 1883; was partly draftsman and afterwards solr.-gen., from Mar. to May, 1887.

DOBERCK, DR. W.—Astronomer in charge of Markree Observ., co. Sligo, 1874-1883; dir. Hong Kong Observ. since 1883; has published twenty volumes of observations and researches in Hong Kong, a pamphlet "On the Law of Storms in the Eastern Seas," and over 200 papers on scientific subjects in transactions of learned societies and scientific periodicals in Europe and America.

DOBSON, HON. ALFRED, C.M.G. (1904).—B. 1848; called to the bar, Inner Tem., Jan., 1875; mem. legis. assem., Tasmania, 1877-87; att.-gen. and mem. exec. coun., 1877; speaker legis. assem., July, 1885; solr.-gen., June, 1887; mem. of coun. of educn., and church advoc. for the diocese of Tasmania; agt.-gen. for Tasmania in London, 1901.

DODDS, THE HON. SIR JOHN STOKELL, K.C.M.G. (1901), KT. BACH., C.M.G. (1889).—B. 1848; att.-gen., Tasmania, Dec., 1878, to Oct., 1879, and in the Giblin ministry, Oct., 1879; col. treas. from Dec., 1881, to Aug., 1884; att.-gen. in the Douglas ministry from Aug., 1884, to Mar., 1886; also premier, Mar. to Dec., 1886; judge, sup. ct., 1886; deleg. col. confee., 1887; ch. just., 1898; admnstr. of govt., 1899, and again 1900-1; lt. gov., 3rd Aug., 1903.

DODDS, WILLIAM JOHN M.D. (Edin.), 1879, gold medallist, M.B. and C.M., 1876; 1st class honours, D.Sc., 1878.—Inspr. of asyls. and med. supt. of Valkenburg asyl., Cape, 1889.

DOHERTY, C. J.—Puiscne judge, super. ct., Quebec, 1891.

DONNAN, J., C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1837; mast. attendant, Colombo, Ceylon, 1863; was comdr. of govt. steamers, "Manchester" and "Pearl," from July 1859; retired, 1902.

DONNELLY, W. J. S.—Survr.-gen., Newfoundland, to 1882; rec.-gen., 1882; resig., 1889; M.L.A. for Placentia, 1893; rec.-gen. and mem. exec. coun., Apr. to Dec., 1894; M.H.A., Placentia, 1897; rec.-gen., 1898; inspir. of cust., 1902.

DONOVAN, JUSTIN FOLEY, M.D., M.CH.L.M.—Med. offr. and health offr., Killcare dispensary, co. Cork, 1876 to 1879; surg., R.N., 1879; received thanks of the admiralty, 1882 and 1888, "for zeal and devotion to duty" at R.N. hosps., Port Royal and Malta; and of the med. dir.-gen., R.N., for professional work, 1882-4-6; retired from the navy 1889; med. attendant, lepers' home, pub. gen. hosp. and constab. training depot, Spanish Town, Jamaica, 1889; med. examr., civ. ser. widows and orphans' pension fund, 1890.

DOUGLAS, ARCHIBALD CAMPBELL.—Ed. Radley Coll. and Oxford Military Coll.; apptd. a consular asst. on the Niger Coast Protec., Dec., 1894; asst. dist. comsnr., Feb., 1896; student, Lincoln's Inn, 1898; transport offr. in Qua Ibo dist. punitive exped., Feb. and Mar., 1899 (West African medal); promoted to rank of 2nd cl. offr., S. Nig., Jan., 1901; served as political offr. with Aro field force, Jan. to Feb., 1902 (medal); dist. comsnr. Brass, 1st Apr., 1904.

DOUGLAS, JAMES ARCHIBALD, M.A.—Director of education, So. Nigeria, Apr., 1903.

DOUGLAS, R. STAIR.—Cadet, Sarawak serv., Nov., 1896; asst. res., June, 1899; res. 2nd cl., Jan., 1902; 2nd cls. res., Baram dist., 1904.

DOUGLAS-DE-FENZI, C. W. P.—Clk. asst. and librarian, Natal; legis. coun., Feb., 1889;
clk., legis. coun., 1893; ag. under-treas., Aug., 1905.

DOWNES, THE HON. SIR J. W., K.C.M.G. (1887), K.C.—B. 1844; att-gen., S. Australia, June, 1881, to June, 1884, and att-gen. and premier, 1885-7; del. to col. confee., 1887; ch. sec. and premier, 1892-3; mem. of senate, Australian parl., 1901-1903; mem. leg. coun., S. Aust., 1905.

DOWNES, MAJOR-GEN. M. FRANCIS, C.M.G. (1885), late R.A.—B. 1834; served in the Crimea till June, 1836, medal and clasp and Turkish medal; instructor of fortificn., R.M.Coll., Sandhurst, for two years; commanded artillery in Mauritius and St. Helena for four years; instructor of gunnery at Woolwich five years; col.-comdt., S. Australia, June, 1877; mem. of roy. coman. on defences, Sydney, 1881; sec. of defence, Victoria, April, 1885, to Mar., 1888; comdt., S. Australian forces, Apr., 1888-92; ret. 1902.

DOWSON, R. W.—Acentnt., Mauritius rly., Sept., 1867; jun. audit examr., June, 1878; ch. clk. rly. dept., Apr., 1882; ag. asst. man., July, 1884, to April, 1885; head accmnt., Sept., 1891; ag. gen. man., July to Sept., 1896; asst. gen. man., July, 1903.

DOYLE, E. A. GAYNES, M.R.C.S., L.R.C.P., Lond.; obstet. soc., Lond.; mem. Br. med. assoc.; late asst. house surg., Westminster hosp.; joined med. service, Trinidad, 1884; ag. dist. med. offr., 1886; res. surg., San Fernando hosp., Nov., 1892; ag. res. surg., col. hosp., Port of Spain, 1893.

DRAKE, THE HON. JAS. GEORGE.—Mem. leg. ass., Queensland, 1888, 1893, 1896, 1899; M.L.C., 12th Dec., 1899; sec. for pub. instn. and P.M.G., Queensland, Dec., 1899, to Feb., 1901; senator for Queensland, Commonwealth parl., Mar., 1901; P.M.G., Commonwealth, Feb., 1901, to Aug., 1903; min. of def., Aug.-Sept., 1903; atty.-gen., Sept., 1903; vice-pres. of ex. coun., 1903; ret. 1906.

DRAKE-BROCKMAN, RALPH EVELYN.—Ed. Elizabeth Coll., Guernsey, Dulwich Coll., and St. George's Hosp.; scholarship, St. George's Hosp., 1st year's proficiency prize and Pollock prize; M.R.C.S. Eng., L.R.C.P. Lond.; apptd. surg.-capt., attached to railway pioneer regt., S.A.F.F., Dec., 1899 (medal and 2 clasps); med. offr., Uganda Prot., 26th Sept., 1900; Suk-Turkana expdttn., 1901 (ment. in desp., spec. ment. by Sir H. Johnston, G.C.M.G., K.C.B., recd. appreciation of serv. from S. of S. for Foreign Affairs); recd. appreciation from S. of S. for the Colonies for serv. during smallpox epidemic in Berbera, Somaliland Prot., 1904-5; med. offr., Somaliland Prot., 6th June, 1904.

DRAYSON, MATTHEW JOHN.—Apptd., after compet. exam., a clerk in the lower (now 2nd) div. of the civ. ser., and assigned to the C.O., May, 1883; asst. registr., May, 1892; promoted to higher grade 2nd div., July, 1896; seconded for service as chief clerk, col. sec.'s off., Hong Kong, 11th Jan., 1902; acted as clk. of coun., Aug., 1902; retd. to C.O. as deputy registr., 22nd July, 1905.

DRAYTON, EDWARD RAWLE, C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1859; clk. col. sec.'s office, Barbados, Sept., 1878; 2nd clk. in office of gov.-in-chief of the Windward Is., July, 1879; ag. ch. clk., May, 1880, and May, 1881, to Jan., 1882; ch. clk., Jan., 1882; ag. col. sec., Grenada, Apr., 1883; priv. sec. to Maj.-gen. Browne, July to Oct., 1884; provost-marshal, ida., Apr., 1885; ag. col. registr., Sept., 1885; regist. sup. ct., J.P., July, 1886; mem. legis. coun., May, 1887; inspr. of prisons, Mar., 1888; mem. exec. coun., Nov., 1888; treas., May, 1890; ag. col. sec., Oct., 1890, to June, 1892; col. sec. and registr.-gen., June, 1892; admstr. govt. of Grenada whenever gov. absent, 1890-1900; govt. of St. Vincent, June, 1893, Feb. to Sept., 1897, and Feb., 1900, to April, 1901; and of Windward Is., Jan., 1897; delegate to W. Indian quarantine conf., Apl., 1904.

DRURY, EDWARD HERBERT MERIVALE.—Trinity Hall, Camb., 1890; called to the bar, Inner Temp., 1896; priv. sec. to Hon. Sir R. G. W. Herbert, G.C.B., Mar., 1899, to June, 1900; priv. sec. to Govr. Sir C. A. Moloney, K.C.M.G., Windward Is., July, 1900; ditto, Trinidad, Dec., 1900, to July, 1902; ch. clk., col. sec.'s office, St. Helena, Oct., 1902; and clk. to ex. coun., Apl., 1903; J.P., Nov., 1902; asst. stip. mag., Nov., 1904.

DRURY, R. FREDERICK, A.M.I.C.E.—Asst. land survr., P.W.D., Hong Kong, 1887; asst. inspr. of bldgs. and asst. sanitary survr., 1888; ag. land survr. and asst. engrnr. on extraordinary pub. wks., 1890; annually recurrent wks., 1892 and 1894; duties in connection with black plague, 1894; ag. sanitary engrnr., 1895; ag. exec. engrnr. for annually recurrent wks., 1897.

DU BOULAY, ED.—Ag. clk. to audr. and treas., St. Lucia, Jan. to May, 1890; 4th clk., treas., Mar. to May, 1892; 3rd clk., May to Dec., 1892; 2nd clk., treas., and accnt., Jan., 1893, to Apr., 1894; ag. ch. clk., treas., Feb. to Nov., 1893; audit clk., Apr., 1894; ag. audr., St. Lucia, Mar. to Sept., 1901; attached to Somerset house for service in W. African colonies, Dec., 1901.

DUDER, T. C.—J.P. Newfoundland, 1874; M.H.A., Fogo, since 1893; financial sec., 1894; chmn. bd. of wks., 1894; survr.-gen. and chmn. bd. of agricul., 1897; min. agricul. and mines, 1898; stip. mag., Bonne Bay, 1901.

DUFF, HECTOR LIVINGSTONE KENNETH.—Asst. collr., B.C. Africa Prot., 1897; resig. from astntr. serv., Nov., 1903; re-apptd., Apr., 1904; collr., Mlanje dist., May, 1904; dist. res., 2nd class, Apr., 1906.

DUFF, GRANT, THE RT. HON. SIR M. E., P.C., G.C.S.I., C.I.E., F.R.S. (1880).—B. 1829; ed. at Balliol Coll., Oxford; B.A. 1850; under-sec. of state for India, 1868 to 1874; lord rector of Aberdeen Univ., 1866 to 1872; parly. under-sec. of state for the cols., Apr., 1880, to Aug., 1881; M.P. for Elgin dist., 1857 to 1881; gov. of Madras, 1881-6.

DUFF, ROBERT.—Record clk., imigrn. dept., Br. Guiana, Apr., 1883; 4th clk., Aug., 1884; 3rd clk., Oct., 1885; 1st class certificate in Hindustani, Mar., 1885; 2nd clk., Mar., 1893; ch. clk., Jan., 1894; has acted as sub.-imigrn. agt. on several occasions, and also as sen. sub.-imigrn. agt.; imigrn. agt. and ch. clk., July, 1898.

DUFFIELD, THOMAS.—Entered crown lands office, S. Australia, Mar., 1867; ch. clk. and imigrn. offr., crown lands and imigrn. dept., 1877; capt. mil. force, 1881; sec. crown lands dept.; mem. of central land and pastoral bds., 1896-1905; sec., crown lands dept., and inspr. of fisheries, Nov., 1901.

DUFFY, THE HON. JOHN GAVAN.—Eldest son of the late Sir Charles Gayan Duffy, Ed. at Stonyhurst. Vice-chancellor's prize, English essay, Melbourne Univ. Succeeded his father in representation of Dalhousie in legis. assem. of Victoria, 1874. Pres. of bd. of land and wks.
of Victoria, 1889; postmr.-gen. of Victoria, 1890; also atty.-gen., 1892; mem. of cabinet without portfolio, 1892; resig. Jan. 1893; again postmr.-gen., 1894.

DUKE, MANSERGH PACE, M.R.C.P., and L.R.C.S.I., L.M. (1875).—Ed. Academic inst., and Meath hosp., Dub.; med. offr., dist. 2, Dominica, 1875 to 1880; asst. surg., Gold Coast, 1880-1; med. offr., dist. 2, Montserrat, May, 1886; offl. mem. legis. coun., Jan., 1888; med. offr., dist. 1, and med. offr. of health, Oct., 1889; mem. exec. coun., Sept., 1895; mem. pub. lib. comtee., Oct., 1896; ex officio mem. bd. of health, Jan., 1897; J.P., Apr., 1897; ag. escheator-gen., July, 1898; holds dormant comsn., July, 1898, to act as comsnr., and has so acted on numerous occasions.

DUKES, HUGH ROBSON.—Asst., Boys' Model Schl., Pietermaritzburg, Natal, 1st Feb., 1893; headmaster, Stanger schl., 1st July, 1895; ag. inspr. of schls., 15th May, 1902 to 30th June, 1903; headmaster, Richmond schl., 1st Oct., 1902; inspr. of schls., 1st July, 1903.

DUMARESQ, ROBT. HARE FITZROY.—Ed. at Haileybury Coll., 1885-1890; matric., New Coll., Oxford, 1890; farming in New Zealand, 1892-99; served in S. African war, 1899-1902 (Queen's medal and two clasps); inspr., land settm., O.R.C., 1902-1906; sec., dept. of agric., O.R.C., 17th Apr., 1906.

DUNBAR, ARTHUR DUNCAN, M.A. (Aberdeen).—Served during S. African war in S. African Light Horse (Queen's and King's medals and clasps); clk. to dir. of educn., Transvaal and O.R.C., 1902-3; priv. sec. to educn. adviser to high comsnr. for S. Africa, 1904-5; clk., educn. dept., O.R.C., 1905.

DUNCAN, ANDREW, H. F. (late lieut. R.N.).—Joined R.N., July, 1868; served in Mediterranean, S. America, Cape, India, Australia, and W. Coast of Africa; resig. Nov., 1883; passed exam. in theoretical survey, July, 1883, and practical survey, 1884, at the Cape Univ., in honours (first of his year on both occasions); from Apr., 1884, employed by the survr.-gen. of the Cape, and in priv. practice; mem. land comsn. of Br. Bechuanaland, Sept., 1885; survr.-gen. of that col., July, 1886; survr.-gen. to Br. S. Africa Co., 1891.

DUNCAN, PATRICK, C.M.G. (1904).—B. 1870; ed. at Oxford, schol. Ball. Coll.; 1st cls. class. mod., 1891; 1st cls. final class. school, 1893; Craven scholarship, 1890; clk., after compet. exam., int. rev., 1894; priv. sec. to Sir A. Milner; prin. clk., 1898; treas., Transvaal, 1901; col. sec., 1st Dec., 1903; mem. ex. and leg. couns.; mem. I.C.C.; ag. liet.-gov., Oct., 1906.

DUNCOMBE, HENRY FEVESHAM.—Entd. col. serv. as an acctnt., treasy., Bahamas, 1891; ag. mag. and coll.; in various dists., 1894-5-6; res. mag., Abaco, 1897; dist. comsnr. Lagos, 1898; has acted on various occasions as pol. mag., collr. of cust., and treas.; passed govt. exam. in Yoruba language, 1900.

DUNCOMBE, W. KELSALL.—2nd clk., tel. dept., Bahamas, Dec., 1905; rev. offr., Inagua, Mar., 1897; asst. res. just., Watlings Island, May, 1900; res. just., Cat Island, July, 1900; supervisor of cust., Lagos, Jan., 1905; ag. collr. of cust., Lagos, from Aug., 1906.

DUNEDIN, 2ND BISHOP OF (founded 1864), Rt. REV. SAMUEL T. NEVILLE, D.D.—Consec. 1871; Magdal. Coll., Camb., B.A. 1865; curate of Scarsbrick, Lancs., 1860-64; rector of Skelton, Staffs., 1864-71; is also primate of New Zealand.

DUNLOP, J. M. M., B.A., LL.D., D.C.L.—Ed. at Trin. Coll., Dublin; barrister-at-law, King's Inn, Dublin, and Inner Temple; dist. comsnr., Lagos, 1900; ag. pol. mag., 1901-2-3; ag. atty.-gen., 1904; ag. ch. asst. col. sec., 1905; ag. atty.-gen., 1906; ditto, S. Nigeria, 1906; ag. judge of sup. ct., S. Nigeria, 1906.

DUNLOP, COLONEL SAMUEL, R.A., C.M.G. (1884)—B. 1838; ag. comsnr. of pol., S. Stiltns., Nov., 1870; ag. pol. mag. and comsnr. of ct. of requests, P.W., Apr., 1871; ag. dep. comsnr. of pol. and coroner, Apl., 1871; ag. dep. comsnr. of pol., Singapore, fire comsnr. and coroner, Aug., 1871; ag. inspr.-gen. of pol., Dec., 1872; comsnr. to Perak, Jan., 1874. In Nov., 1874, comsnr. with the forces sent to quell the disturbances in the native state of Sungai Ujong; inspr.-gen., Straits pol., May, 1875. In Nov., 1875, on the murder of Mr. Birch, apptd. special comsnr. (temporarily) for Perak affairs; organized the expdn. which captured the Passir Salak stockades, and was present at the capture, Nov., 1875; comsnr. to forces during operations in Perak, Dec., 1875; accompanied Gen. Colborne's force up the Perak river, and across country to Kinta; ag. res. coun., Penang, 1884 to 1885; pres. of Singapore mun. comsn., 1889; ret., 1890.

DUNN, ROBERT ERNST.—Clerk and interp. to the R.M., Umgeni div., Natal, 1880; to R.M., Lions River, Mar., 1883; to R.M., Alfred, Oct., 1887; to R.M., Upper Umkomanzi, 1894; mag. for Colony, mag., Weenen div., 1901.

DUNN, STEPHEN TROYTE, F.L.S.—Ed. Radley and Merton Coll., Oxford; B.A., 1889; asst. for India, Kew Gdns., 1899; sup., bot. and forestry dept., Hong Kong, 1903; J.P., 1906.

DUNRAVEN AND MOUNT-EARL (4th Earl of), WINDHAM THOMAS WINDHAM-QUIN, K.P.—B. 1841; partly, under-sec. of state for the cols., June, 1885, to Feb., 1886, and again Aug., 1886, to Feb., 1887.

DUNSMUIR, JAMES.—B. 1851; elec. to legislature of B. Columbia, 1898; premier, 1900 to 1902, when he resig.; lieut.-gov. of B. Columbia, 11th May, 1906.

DUPIGNY, E. G. MORSON.—Asst. govt. off., Dominica, Feb., 1889; clk. comsnrs. of valuatin., 1890; clk. mag., dist. F., 1890; do., presit.'s off. Dom., 1890-92; do. regtr.'s off., 1892; do. treas., Antigua, 1896; stud. Mid. Temp., 1900.

DUPONT, LOUIS EVENOR.—4th clk., registry, sup. ct., Mauritius, 1st Sept., 1864; ch. clk., regsn. dept., 18th June, 1884; recvr. of regsn. dues and conservator of mortgages, 6th May, 1901.

DURMAN, F. J.—Apptd., after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. serv., and assigned to C.O., 15th April, 1901.

DU VERGE, L. S. R., I.S.O. (1903).—Inspr. of distilleries, Mauritius, 1868; ag. registr.-gen., 1896-7; storekeeper-gen., June, 1897; ag. recvr.-gen., in 1901, 1902 and 1903; nom. mem. of coun. of govt.

DUVIVIER, AIMÉ.—Clk., archives office, Mauritius, 1st Nov., 1879; custodian of archives, 1st Jan., 1891.

DYER, JAMES HAROLD.—Ed. King William's Coll., I. of Man, King Edward VI. schl., Berkhamstead; recd. his comsn. in 3rd Batt. S. Lanc. regmt., 1889; obtained his compny., 1893; resig. comsn., 1894; joined Matabele relief force, 1896, and served through the campaign till the force was disbanded in 1897; joined C.M.R., 1897, and served through siege of Mafeking; resig. Cape Police in July, 1901; received medals and clasps;
apptd. asst. dist. comsnr. S. Nigeria, 28th Dec., 1901; ag. dist. comsnr., Ediba, 1902.

DYER, THOS. T. R.—Entd. pub. ser. of St. Vincent as cust. offr., Jan., 1890; ag. clk., treasy., 1891; asst. clk., P.O., 2nd clk. gov. off. to Apl., 1892; ag. 2nd clk. in off. of gov., Windward Islds., May, 1892; transf. to St. Lucia; 4th clk., treasy., May, 1892; 3rd clk., Jan., 1893; ag. 2nd clk., Feb. to May, 1893; 2nd clk., govt. off., May, 1893; also supt. of govt. printing; ag. 2nd clk. in off. of adminstr., Wind. Islds., 1894; hurricane relic offr., St. Vincent, Sept. to Dec., 1898; ag. ch. clk. and clk. of couns., St. Lucia, Oct., 1900, to Mar., 1901; agptd. ch. clk. to gov. Windward Is. (Grenada), 1st Apr., 1901; ch. clk., col. sec.'s office, and clk. of ex. and leg. couns., 16th Nov., 1902.

DYER, SIR WILLIAM T. THISELTON, M.A., F.R.S., K.C.M.G. (1899), C.M.G. (1882).—B. 1843; Chr. Ch., Oxon, 1873; asst. dir., Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, 1873; dir., 1885; ret., 1905; botan. adviser to S. of S. for Col.

DYETT, EDWARD F.—2nd treasy. offr., Montserrat, Aug., 1886; admeasurer of vessels, 1889; 1st treasy. offr., June, 1891; comsnr. oaths, Nov., 1895; clk. of waterworks comsnrs., 1896; sec. bd. of health, Jan., 1897; held a comsnr., Dec., 1897, to act as treas. of Montserrat in absence of comsnr., and so acted on numerous occasions until Jan., 1900, when authorised by law to perform duties of treas. in conjunction with those of 1st treasy. offr.; J.P., May, 1898; offl. rec. in bankruptcy, Aug., 1898; holds comsnr., dated Feb., 1899, to admnr. oaths of office to ag. comsnr. in absence of comsnr. and govrn.; mem. legis. coun., Mar., 1900; visiting just. of prison, Nov., 1900; ag. col. postmnr., Antigua, Nov., 1903.

DYETT, HENRY.—Served in P.O. and treasy., Montserrat, Mar., 1894, to Feb., 1896; sec. valuation comsnrs., 1895; clk. to Mr. E. Baynes, comsnr. and mag., Montserrat, and to exec. coun., Feb., 1896, also to Mr. F. H. Watkins, I.S.O., 1900, and to Lt.-Col.W.B.Davidson-Houston,1906; ag. 2nd treasy. offr., Apr., May and Sept., 1897; clk., legis. coun., Mar., 1898; ag. 2nd treasy. and quarantine offr., July, 1902, to Apr., 1903; ag. jun. audit clk., Antigua, Oct.-Nov., 1903; sec., valuation comsnrs., Montserrat, 1904; govt. offr., St. Kitts, Nov., 1906.

DYETT, RICHARD HENRY KORTRIGHT.—Served in pres.'s office, Virgin Is., 1879 to 1881, and 1882 to 1884; clk. regis.'s office, Nevis, 1886; 2nd clk. regis.'s office, Antigua, 1887; clk. to trustee, supt. ct. lib., July, 1888; comsnr. to admnr. oaths, 1889; marshal V.A. ct., L.I., Dec., 1889; clk. to mag., dist. A., 1890; dep. cor., dist. A., 1892; ag. postmnr., May to Sept., 1894; 1st clk. regis.'s offr., Jan., 1895; dep. cor., dist. B., Oct., 1896; ag. mag., dist. A., Jan., Feb., Apl., to Nov., 1897; sec. to H.M. Diamond Jubilee comte., June, 1897; ag. mag., dist. B., Apl., 1898, to Jan., 1899; ag. mag., dist. B., May to Sept., 1899; and 25th Oct., 1899; ag. mag., dist. A., Nov., 1899, to May, 1900; during which period (Jan. to Apl.) acted also as mag., dist. B.; ag. mag., dist. A., June, 1900, to Mar., 1901; and Apl. to Nov., 1901; also in Mar., 1902; mem. of "Coronation" comte., and hon. sec. to same, May, 1902; ag. mag., dist. A., Aug., 1902, to Feb., 1903; regis. and prov.-marshal and regis. of titles, St. Kitts-Nevis, 11th June, 1903; mem. of Basseterre town bd., June, 1903; regis. and prov.-marshal, Antigua, and ch. regis., Leeward Is., July, 1905; trustee, sup. ct. library, Aug., 1905.

EAKIN, JAS. W.—B.A., M.D., M. Ch. Univ., Dublin; govt. med. offr., Trinidad; dist. med. offr., Port of Spain, S., and consulting surg. Col. hosp., San Fernando; surg.-major, local force.

EARL, ROBT. STEPHEN, M.A., M.B., B.C. (Cantab., 1891).—Med. offr. Lasoyedist., Dominica, Jul., 1892; med. offr., No. 5 dist. Antigua, 1896; comsnr. Virgin Is.

EARNSHAW, ALBERT.—Ed. at Univ. Coll., Durham, and Pemb. Coll., Oxford; held foundtn.; Newby and Univ. class. schlrships., Durham, 1885-1887; 1st cls. classics, 1st year exam., 1886; 1st cls. class. final, 1887; B.A., 1887; M.A., 1890; elected fellow of Durham, 1889; open class. schlr., Pemb. Coll., Oxford, Jan., 1888; 1st cls. class. mods., 1889; 2nd cls. lit. hum., 1891; B.A., Oxford, 1891; called to the bar, Inner Tem., 1893; went N.E. circuit and W. Riding, Yorks, sessions, etc., 1893-1904; common law lecturer, Yorks. Coll., Leeds, 1899-1900; pol. mag. and coroner, W. div., Grenada, Feb., 1904; ditto S. (or 1st) div., and escheator-gen., Grenada, June, 1905.

EASTERBROOK, ARTHUR DOVE.—Asst. collr., B.Cent. Africa Prot., June, 1896; 2nd cls. asst., May, 1902; dist. mag. and collr., N. Nyasa, May, 1904.

EATON, HENRY FRANCIS.—Clk., col. storekeeper's office, Melbourne, Jan., 1853; transf. to civil commissariat, Feb., 1854; acctnt., govt. stores, Feb., 1855; transf. to treasy., Mar., 1865; ag. acctnt., treasy., 1869-70, 1876, 1886-7; acctnt. to treasy., 1887; under treas., Sept., 1889—1895; capt. volr. artillery, 1876; is in the commission of the peace of the Colony.

EDWARDS, COL. ALFRED HAMILTON MACKENZIE, C.B.—Served in 1st Dragoon Guards, Jan., 1883, to Apl., 1892; adjutant, Behar Light Horse Volunteers, India, Apl., 1892, to Apl., 1897; 1st and 5th Dragoon Guards and Imperial Light Horse, Apl., 1897, to Oct., 1900; Hazara (N.-W. Frontier, India), 1888, asst. prov. marshal (ment. in desp., medal and clasp); commanded Imperial Light Horse, S. African war, Nov., 1899, to June, 1900; dist. comsnr., Potchefstroom and Krugersdorp dists., June to Oct., 1900; commanded "A" division, S.A.C., Oct., 1900, to end of war (ment. in desp., Queen's medal, 4 clasps, King's medal, 2 clasps); substantive lt.-col. in the army, dated 29th Nov., 1900; commdt., Transvaal volunteer; left the service, 1906.

EDWARDS, CHAR. HENRY.—Ed. St. Bees gram. schl. and Queen's Coll., Oxford; exhibtn. of Queen's Coll., B.A., 1894; B.C.L., 1901; called to the bar, Mid. Tem., 1898; dist. comsnr., G. Coast, Dec., 1899; dist. and stip. mag., Mauritius, 1904.

EGERTON, RICHARD.—Ed. Westminster and Chr. Ch., Oxford; B.A. 1867; called to the bar, Mid. Tem., Nov., 1869; asst. res. mag., Kingston, May, 1892; res. mag., Jamaica, Feb., 1893.

EGERTON, SIR WALTER, K.C.M.G. (1905), C.M.G. (1901).—B. 1858; ed. Tonbridge Schl.; cadet, S. Sttlmts., Oct., 1880; asst. to the Chinese prot., Jan., 1881; mag., Singapore, Jan., 1881; passed final exam, Malay, May, 1882; colr. of land rev., Penang and P.W., Jan., 1883; 2nd mag. of pol., Penang, May, 1883; also official assignee under the Bankruptcy Ordinance (Sept., 1882); ag. sen. dist. offr. Butterworth, P.W., Apl., 1890; a J.P. and coroner for S. Sttlmts., and a visiting justice for Penang; offr. in char., Sungel Ujong, July, 1893; ag. res., Pahang, May to July, 1894; offl. assignee and regis. of deeds, Singapore, June, 1896; inspr. of prisons, S. Sttlmts., May, 1897; dep.-pres.of
mun. comsrs., Singapore, Mar., 1897; 1st mag., Penang, Apr., 1897; ag. 1st mag., Singapore, Jan., 1898; ag. res. councillor, Malacca, Mar., 1898, and Mar., 1899; 1st mag., Singapore, Oct., 1898, but continued to act as res. coun.; ag. col. treas., S.S., Nov.-Dec., 1898; ag. col. sec., S.S., Apr., 1900; ag. res. councilr., Penang, Feb. to Apr., 1901; ag. col. treas., S.S., Aug.-Oct., 1902; res., Neg. Semb., Aug., 1902; high commr., S. Nigeria, Nov., 1903; and gov., Lagos, 30th July, 1904.

EGGETT, W. H.—Apptd., after a compet. exam., to be a clk. of the lower (now 2nd) div. of the civ. ser., and assigned to the C.O. Nov., 1880; promoted to higher grade, 2nd div., Apr., 1896; asst. accntnt., 6th Apr., 1899.

EHRHARDT, ALBERT.—Ed. King Edward's High Schl., B'ham, and Worc. Coll., Oxford; graduated with honours in mods. and lit. hum., 1886; Inner Tem. schrshp., common law, 1888; called to bar, 1889; dist. comsrs., Lagos, 1896; travelling comsrs. on the E. bndry., Aug., 1897; ag. res. of Ibadan, 1898; ag. treas. and mem. exec. and legis. couns., June, 1900; ag. att.-gen., Sept., 1900; rlyv. comsrs. at Aro, June, 1901; ag. treas., Aug., 1901, to Mar., 1902; ag. atty.-gen., Mar. to June, 1902; apptd. res., Ibadan, Feb., 1902; apptd. col. treas., May, 1902; atty.-gen., Fjiji, mem. ex. and leg. couns., May, 1903; ag. ch. just., May, 1904; apptd. as comsrs. to produce revised edition of ordinances of the colony, 1903; ag. ch. just., May to Oct., 1904.

ELCUM, JOHN BOWEN, B.A., Oxon.—Ed. Highgate Schl. and Queen's Coll., Oxford; scholar of Queen's Coll., 1878; cadet, S. Stltmsts., Oct., 1884; passed in Malay, 1886; ag. dist. offr., S. Malacca, 1887; dist. offr. Bukit Mertajam, P.W., Jan., 1890; ag. dist. offr., Dindings, Dec., 1890; sheriff, Penang, Mar., 1892; ag. sheriff, Singapore, June, 1893; 2nd mag., Penang, Nov., 1893; ag. collr. land revenue, Singapore, Dec., 1893, to Feb., 1894; ag. inspr. of schls., S. Stltmsts., June, 1895; also ag. official assignee and regir. of deeds, Singapore, Mar. to June, 1896; collr. of land rev. and offr. in charge of treasy., July, 1897; ag. 1st mag., Singapore, Mar., 1898; inspr. of schls., Aug., 1898, but continued to act as first mag. till Feb., 1899; dir. pub. instrn., Aug., 1901; inspr. of prisons, July, 1904; fin. comsrs., F.M.S., Oct., 1904; dir. of pub. instruction, S. Stltmsts. and F.M.S., 1906.

ELDRIDGE, A. E. G.—Clk., P.O., Antigua, Mar., 1880; clk. to pres. and isld. sec. and clk. to exec. coun., 1882; postmr. of Antigua, Aug., 1891; ag. mag. and coroner, Dist. B., 1894, 1896, and 1897; ag. mag. and coroner, Dist. H., Nevis, Apr., 1896, to Feb., 1900; mem. St. Kitts-Nevis legis. coun., and gen. legis. coun., 1899; ag. comsrs., of Virgin Is., and ag. asst. col. sec., Leeward Is., 1903.

ELFFERS, PIETER.—T. ii. (Holland), T. i. (O.F.S.); ed. at Normal Training Coll., Nymeyer, Holland; Dutch mast., pub. schl., Stellenbosch, 1882-84; ditto, Grey Coll. Schl., 1884-93; prin., govt. schl., Fauresmith, 1893-1901; Dutch mast., boy's high schl., Wynberg, Cape Colony, 1901-03; ditto, pub. schl., Bethulie, 1903-04; ditto, pub. schl., Winburg, 1904-05; inspr. of schls., O.R.C., 1st July 1905.

ELGEE, CAPT. C. H.—B. 1871; ed. Lancing and Sandhurst; 1st coms., 16th Foot, Feb., 1892; capt., Oct., 1899; active service, Chitra, 1896 (medal with clasp); Ashanti campaign, relief of Kumasi, 1900 (medal); adjutant, Lagos Haussa Force, 1899; A.D.C. and priv. sec. to Sir W. Macgregor, gov. of Lagos, 1900 to 1902; and clk. of ex. coun.; ag. insp.-gen., 1902; trav. comsrs., Lagos, 1902; ag. col. treas., mem. of ex. and leg. couns., 1902; resident, Ibadan, 1st Jan., 1903; author of "Memo. on Negro Education."

ELGIN AND KINCARDINE, 9th Earl of (creat. 1633), VICTOR ALEXANDER BRUCE, K.G. (creat. 1899); G.C.S.I., G.C.LE., P.C., LL.D., D.C.L.; Baron Bruce, 1603; Earl of Kincardine and Baron Bruce of Torry, 1647; Baron Elgin (U.K.), 1849.—B. 1849; ed. Eton and Balliol Coll., Oxford, M.A.; treas. of Household and 1st comsrs. of wks., 1886; Lord-Lieut. of Fifeshire since 1885; Viceroy of India, 1894-99; chrmn. Roy. Coms. on S. African War, 1892; chrmn., Roy. Coms. on Free Churches Controversy in Scotland, 1904; chrmn. Roy. Coms. to administer Scottish Churches Act, 1905; sec. of state for the Colonies, Dec., 1905.

ELIOT, EDWARD CARLYON.—Ed. Bradfield Coll. and Uppingham; apptd. 5th class clk., govt. secretariat, British Guiana, 1895; seconded ag. clk. to govt. agent, N.-W. dist., Br. Guiana, for periods 1896 to 1899; 4th class clk., govt. secretariat, 1899; pay and quartermr. to Hausa force, Gold Coast Col., 1900; apptd. senior ast. treas., Oct., 1902; dist. comsrs., G. Coast, 5th May, 1905.

ELLIOT, LAURENCE S., I.S.O. (1903).—B. 1845; clk. to mags., W. Australia; landing and tide waiter at Bunbury, 1863; also postmr. and ast. dist. registr.; clk. in col. sec.'s office, 1872; sec. to central bd. of educn. and ast. clk. in legia. coun., 1873; registr.-gen., registr. of deeds, and registr. of brands, 1876; ag. ch. clk., col. sec.'s dept., Jan., 1878, to Jan., 1880; 1st clk. and registr.-gen., col. sec.'s dept., Jan., 1880; apptd. to take the census, Apr., 1881, and to superintend its compilation; ch. clk. and accntnt., treasy., Apl., 1881; ag. astt., col. sec., Dec., 1889, to Oct., 1890; under treas., Jan., 1891; is a J.P.

ELLENBERGER, JULES.—Clk. to ast. comsrs., Bech. Prot., 1890; interpreter to concessions coman., Bech. Prot., 1893; ditto to Sir S. Shippard's boundy. comsn., 1894; J.P., 1893; astt. mag., 1898; served in S. African war, including relief of Mafeking; spec. comsrs. for oaths of allegiance in So. dist. of Bech. Prot. to burghers of late S.A.R. and O.F.S.; astt. comsrs., So. dist., Bech. Prot., 11th July, 1902.

ELLERY, R. L. J., F.R.S., C.M.G. (1889).—B. 1827; astronomer, Victoria, 1853.

ELLIOT, MAJOR SIR HENRY GEORGE, K.C.M.G. (1899), C.B. (1901), C.M.G. (1879).—B. 1826; ch. mag. of Tembuland, C. of Good Hope; in command of Tembu levies during Basuto war; ret., 1904.

ELLIOTT, SIR CHARLES BLETTERTAN, LL.B., K.C.M.G. (1901), C.M.G. (1894).—B. 1841; clk., col. sec.'s office, Cape, 1859; clk. to Justice Watermeyer, 1863; sec. to examrs. in literature and science; clk., col. sec.'s office, 1867; ch. clk. dept. of lands and wks., Dec., 1872; advoc.sup., 1873; astt. comsrs., crown lands and pub. wks., 1876; gen. manager, rlys., Dec., 1880; is mem. of coun. of Univ., Cape; examr. and moderator of examrs. in science; ret., 1904.

ELLIOTT, COL. JOHN, R.M.L.I., C.B. (1877), C.M.G. (1891).—B. 1824; entered R.N. in 1838; 2nd lieut., June, 1846; col., 1869; served in the China expdn., 1842 (medal); served in H.M.S. "Fox" during the Burmese war, 1852 (officially thanked); mentioned in despatches; commd. the Royal Marines in the steam flotilla on the Irrawaddy (mentioned in gov.gen.'s despatch; medal with clasp for Pegu). Served at the bombardment and surrender of the forts of Bomarsund, in Aug.,
1854 (Baltic medal), and during the siege of Sebastopol in 1855, the expdn. to Kertch and Yeni-Kale (medal with clasp, 5th class of the Medjidie, and Turkish medal); has also the medal for the Kaffir war. Served as maj. of brigade to the force of Royal Marines landed in Mexico in 1863; lieut.-col., Devonshire Rifle Volr. Corps, 1870; in 1871 J.P. for Plymouth; in 1874 called to the bar, Mid. Temp., and joined the western circuit; in 1876 inspr. of prisons and stip. J.P., Br. Guiana; inspr.-gen. of pol., Barbados, 1881; adminstd. govt. of St. Vincent, 1884 and 1889; acted as col. sec., Barbados, 1886 and 1894; ret. 1895.

ELLIS, FRANCIS ROBT., C.M.G.—B. 1849; writer in the Ceylon civ. ser., July, 1871; additional pol. mag., Kurunegala, 1874; office asst. to gov't. agt. N. Prov., 1876; ag. pol. mag., Kandy, 1878; ag. asst. agt. Matale, 1879; ditto, Mullaitivu, 1880; dist. judge, Ratnapura, 1st Apr., 1883; pol. mag., Colombo, 1885; dir. and inspr.-gen. of prisons, 1891-6; ag. inspr.-gen. pol., May to Nov., 1893; ag. prin. collr. of cust., Jan., 1896; gov't. agt., S. prov., Jan. to Mar., 1897; gov't. agt., W. prov., Sept., 1897; aud.-gen., Mar., 1902; ag. col. sec., 19th Nov., 1903; ret.

ELLIS, FRANK THOS.—Cadet, S. Sttlmts., 27th Nov., 1903.

ELLIS, WALTER DEVONSHIRE.—Ed. at Winchester and New Coll., Oxon; scholar, 1890-1895; prox. acc. Hertford Univ. scholarship, 1891; 1st class classical mods., 1892; Univ. jun. Greek testament prize, 1893; 1st class literae humaniores, 1894; B.A., 1894; M.A., 1897; chancellor's prize, Latin essay, 1895; apptd., after compet. exam., to be a clk. in the C.O., Apr., 1895; priv. sec. to Lord Selborne, June, 1897; 1st class clk., 1899.

ELLIS, WILLIAM GILMORE, M.D., M.R.C.S.—Med. supt., lunatic asylum, Singapore, 1888; ag. also as municipal health offr., Singapore, May, 1889, to Feb., 1892, again 1894; ag. col. res. surg. in 1901, 1902 and 1903.

ELY, HERBERT WILLIAM.—Clk. in dept. of agt.-gen. for Tasmania; ch.clk., 1895; sec., 1899; acted as priv. sec. to Rt. Hon. Sir Edward Braddon, P.C., K.C.M.G., ex-premier of Tasmania, during his visit to England for the Diamond Jubilee celebration, 1897.

EMERSON, Geo. H.Y. K.C.—Speaker, house of assem., Newfoundland, 1890-94; mem. of official delegation to London, 1890, and of delegation from legislature in 1891 on the fisheries question; mem. exec. coun., 1895; asst. judge, sup. ct., Nov., 1896.

EMMENS, JOHN HOWARD.—Apptd., after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser., and assigned to C.O., 11th Mar., 1901.

EMMS, C. B.—Clk., G.P.O., O.R.C., Aug., 1902; clk., treasy., Oct., 1903; asst. acctnt., funds dept., July, 1905.

EMTAGE, O. DE C., M.A.—Ed. Harr. Coll., Barbados; Barbados scholar, 1886; scholar, Worc. Coll., Oxon, 1887; 1st class math. mods., 2nd cls. finals, 1890; hon. nat. sc. schools, 1891; asst. mast., Harr. Coll., 1891; examiner, 2nd grade schools, Barbados, 1891-1902; ditto, gram. school, St. Lucia, 1894-95; ditto, Grenada, 1897-98; head master. The Lodge school, 1899.

EMTAGE, WM. THOS. ALDER, M.A., Oxford; Fell. of Phys. Soc., Lond.; ed. Harrison Coll., Barbados; scholar, Pembroke Coll., Oxford, 1880; 1st cls. math. mods., 1881; 1st cls. final maths., 1883; 1st cls. nat. sci., 1885; University Coll., Nottingham, math. lecturer, 1885; asst. prof. math. and phys., 1889; prof. maths. and phys., 1891; principal, tech. inst., Wandsworth (L.C.C.), 1895; director of pub. instn., Mauritius, 1900; examnr., Oxford Locals, maths., 1888, 1889; examnr., final hon. school nat. sci., Oxford, 1890, 1891; author of "Mathematics of Electricity" (Oxford Press), and other works.

ENGELBACH, A. H. H., I.S.O. (1902).—B. 1850; apptd., 29th Dec., 1869, after passing an exam. before the civ. ser. comsrs., clk.in the acctns. branch in the office of the sec. of state for the colo., having acted in that capacity since Mar., 1868; 1st class asst. clk., 1st Sept., 1879; bookkeeper and sen. asst. to the financial clk., 1884; acted for financial clk., June, 1886, to Apr., 1887; accountant, Apr., 1896.

ENNIS, GEORGE FRANCIS MACDANIEL.—Ed. at King's Coll. school and privately; called to the bar, Mid. Temp., Jan., 1892; sec. to gov', B.N. Borneo, 13th Nov., 1894; session judge, B.N. Borneo and Labuan, 24th Dec., 1894; judge of general ct., Labuan, 1895; judge of chief ct., B.N. Borneo, 14th Aug., 1895; ag. res., Province Alcock, B.N. Borneo, 13th Dec., 1895; resig., Oct., 1897; ag. asst. judge, Zanzibar, 18th May to 7th July, and 1st Aug. to 24th Oct., 1899; registr., E. Africa Prot., 1st Oct., 1899; town mag., Mombasa, 20th July, 1900; ag. judge, E. Africa Prot., 6th Sept., 1900; ag. asst. judge, Zanzibar, 25th Jan., 1901; legal vice-consul, Uganda Prot., 1st Jan., 1902; judge of high ct. of Uganda, 11th Aug., 1902, and judge of H.B.M. Court of Appeal for Eastern Africa.

ENRAGHT-MOONY, F.—Sub-inspr., Basutoland police, Mar., 1884; acted as gov't. sec., Basutoland, 1893-1895; commanded Bech. Prot. native police with rank of capt., 1896; asst. comsrr., Basutoland, 1897; acted as gov't. sec., 1900-1901; mentioned in com.-in-chief's desps., 1901; native comsrr., Zoutpansberg, Aug., 1901; commanded Ft. Edward and Spelonken dist., Northern Transvaal, and acted as intell. offr. until close of war; special comsrr., Swaziland, June, 1902; res. mag. and native comsrr., Swazi-land, 1905.

ESNOUF, E. AMAND.—Dist. mag., Seychelles, 1870; Grand Port, Mauritius, 15 May, 1878; dist. mag., Moka, 1883; jun. dist. mag., Port Louis, Aug., 1884; ag. master sup. ct., May, 1886; and Dec., 1887, to Jan., 1888; ag. sen. dist. mag., Pt. Louis, Mar., 1890, to Mar., 1892; Dec., 1892, to Feb., 1893; May to Aug., 1896; ag. dist. mag., Pt. Louis, 3rd div., Feb., 1898; ag. dist. and stip. mag. Riv. du Rempart, Mar., 1898; dist. mag., Pt. Louis, 3rd div., Mar., 1899; ag. substitute mast. sup. ct., Aug., 1901.

EVANS, SIR DAVID, K.C.M.G. (1892).—B.1849; Lord Mayor of London, 1891-2; raised funds for relief of distress caused by the Mauritius hurricane and the fire at St. John's, Newfoundland.

EVANS, FREDERICK, C.M.G. (1881), C.V.O. (1903).—B. 1849; entered the civ. ser., Admiralty, Somerset house, 13th Dec., 1867; transf'd. to the sec.'s dept. at Whitehall, Jan., 1872; asst. col. sec. and treas., S. Leone, May, 1878; priv. sec. to Sir S. Rowe, K.C.M.G., Feb., 1879, to Feb., 1881; ag. clk. of legis. coun., Sept., 1879; acted as col. sec., Dec., 1879, to Feb., 1880; ch. sec. and ch. of the staff to Sir S. Rowe during threatened hostilities with Ashanti, 1881; asst. col. sec., G. Coast, 1882; ag. clk. of customs and treas., Oct., 1882, to Jan., 1883; ag. col. sec., Aug. to Dec., 1883, and on other occasions; clk. of legis. coun., Feb., 1882, to Apr., 1884; dep. gov', Lagos, July to Aug., 1883, and May, 1885, to Jan., 1886; dep. gov', G. Coast, Sept., 1883, and Apr., 1885; col. sec., Lagos, Jan., 1886; ag. admnstr., July, 1886; col.
sec., G. Coast, 1887; Leeward Is., 1888; Jamaica, 1896; ag. 1st cl. clk., C.O., Feb., 1900; col. sec., Gibraltar, 1901.

EVANS, HON. JOHN WM., C.M.G. (1906).—B. 1855; M.L.A. for Kingborough, Tasmania, since 1896; warden and master warden of marine bd.of Hobart for many years; premier of Tasmania, July, 1904.

EVANS, WILLIAM.—Cadet, S. Sttlmts., Nov., 1882; ed. King's Coll., Camb.; ag. astt. protector of Chinese, Singapore, Dec., 1885; ag. collr. of land rev., Malacca, May, 1886; 2nd astt. prot. of Chinese, May, 1887; ag. astt. prot. Chinese, Singapore, Feb., 1888; ag. 2nd mag., Penang, July, 1888; passed exams. in Chinese and Malay; J.P.; ag. dist. offr., Dindings, 1888; astt. prot. of Chinese, Singapore, June, 1890; ag. prot. of Chinese, Penang, July, 1890; ditto, S. Sttlmts., Nov. and Dec., 1891, to June, 1893; astt. prot. Chinese, Penang, 1893; prot. of Chinese, S. Sttlmts., Apr., 1895; ag. audr.-gen., S.S., May, 1901, to July, 1902; pres., municipal comsrs., Singapore, Sept., 1903; seconded for 6 mos. spec. serv. in Transvaal as prot. of Chinese, 25th Dec., 1903; ag. res. coun., Malacca, Mar., 1906.

EVELYN, EDWARD A.—2nd clk. to regtr., St. Kitts, 1899; govt. offr., Sandy Point, Apr., 1903; govt. offr., Dieppe Bay, St. Kitts, June, 1905; clk., regtr.'s off., May, 1906.

EVELYN, EDWARD ERNEST.—Ed. Harrison Coll., Barbados; ent. col. sec.'s off., Barbados, 1883; astt. clk., govt. savings bk., 1883; ch. clk., 1884; rev. offr., St. Lucia, Jan., 1885, to Nov., 1890; accnt., P.W.D., Nov., 1890, to Jan., 1893; audit clk., Jan., 1893, to Mar., 1894; ch. clk., govt. off., and clk. of coun., Apl., 1894; astt. col. sec., S. Leone, Nov., 1900.

EVELYN, E. F.—Acentnt. of post office, Barbados, Sept., 1880.

EVELYN, MERRIT.—2nd clk. to pres., St. Kitts, Dec., 1878; ch. clk., treasy., Nevis, 1881; ag. treas., Nevis, July, 1882-1883; rev. offr. in charge, Nevis, treasy., 1883; prot. of imgrts., Nevis, 1883; land and house tax comsrs., 1892; ag. mag., Nevis, 1894-5, 1895-6; water comsrs., Nevis, 1901; mem. quarantine bd., Nevis, 1903.

EVERARD, W.—Supernum. col. sec.'s office, Barbados, Sept., 1868; landing waiter, customs, Dec., 1868; ag. inspr. of inl. rev. offrs., Jan., 1884, to Dec., 1885; ch. clk., P.O., Mar., 1886; sen. landing waiter, customs, June, 1886.

EVERETT, COL. SIR W., K.C.M.G.—B. 1844; apptd. one of Brit. comsrs. in Paris for settlement of W. African affairs, 1895-1898.

EVERY, THE REV. EDWARD FRANCIS, M.A.—Bishop of the Falklands, 1902.

EWING, HON. THOMAS THOMSON.—M.L.A. for Richmond, N.S. Wales, 1885-94; ditto for Lismore, 1894-1901; some time chrmn. of parl'y. pub. wks. comttee., N.S. Wales; retd. to 1st house of rep., C. of Aust., Mar., 1901; re-elected Dec., 1903; vice-pres. of exec. coun., July, 1905; min. of home affairs, 13th Oct., 1906.

EYLES, C. H.—Asst. col. surg., G. Coast Col., 1883; col. surg., Br. Honduras, 1887.

EZECHIEL, P. H.—B.A., Bombay, 1889 (at 14); first in Woolwich competn., 1893; B.A., London, 1894 (2nd exhibn. at matric., 1892); major schlr., Trin. Coll., Camb., 1896; 4th wrangler and B.A., Camb., 1897; apptd. after compet. exam., 2nd cl. clk., C.O., 11th Oct., 1898; passed final exam. for Bar, 1902; sec. to Crown agts. for the Colonies, May, 1905.

FABRE, HECTOR, C.M.G. (1887).—B. 1834; formerly senator, Canada; hon. comsrs. for Canada, Ind. and Col. exhibn.; now Canadian agt., Paris.

FACEY, LUTHER HERBERT.—3rd cl. clk., prisons dept., Jamaica, June, 1877; 2nd cl. clk., June, 1879; 1st cl. clk., police and prisons dept., Nov., 1892.

FAGAN, JOSEPH PATRICK.—L.R.C.S., L.R.C.P., L.M., Ireland; dip. trop. med.; dist. med. offr., Niger Coast Prot., 13th Apl., 1894; served in operations agst. Chief Nana, Benin River, 1894, (spec. ment. in desps., medal and clasp); served in operations agst. King of Benin, 1897, and Aro field force 1901 (medal and clasp); senior med. offr., 29th May, 1903; ag. dep. P.M.O., 1905.

FAIRBAIRN, JOHN.—Temporary clk. in leg. coun. off., Cape Town, Apr., 1881 to 30th Apr., 1889; crown lands off., 31st May, 1890, to 31st July, 1891; clk., to regtr. of mines, Prince Albert, 1st Aug., 1891, to 31st May, 1892; leg. coun. off., 1st June, 1892, to 30th Sept., 1893, and 1st Jan. to 31st May, 1899; clk. of the papers and comtce. clk., 1st July, 1899; clk. astt. and taxing offr., 1st Jan., 1904; hon. sec., Central Good Hope Red Cross comttee., Victoria League for concentration camp relief, etc., etc.; is an esquire of the order of St. John of Jerusalem, in England, 1901; S. African War medal and clasp, 1899-1901.

FAIRBAIRN, ROBERT, I.S.O. (1906).—Second master, boys' schl., Perth, W. Australia, 1859; clk. to bench of mags., landing waiter, and postmr., Vasse, 1862; res. mag., mag. of local ct., and dist. regisr., 1875; Newcastle, 1875; Vasse, 1880; Kimberley, 1883; Fremantle, 1886.

FALCK, DAVID GEORGE ANOSI.—Joined post and tel. dept., O.F.S., Nov., 1881; postmr. and telegraphist, Winburg, Nov., 1881; landdrost's clk., Bethlehem, Aug., 1889; ag. landdrost, Heilbron, Apl., 1890; sec., G.P.O., O.F.S., Aug., 1892; landdrost, Ficksburg, 1894 (not assumed); postmr.-gen., O.F.S., 1st Jan., 1895; ditto, O.R.C., Mar., 1900.

FALSHAW, PERCY SCOTT.—M.R.C.V.S., Govt. vet. surgeon, Singapore, S. Sttlmts., 15th June, 1893.

FARRAR, NICHOLAS.—Supernum., P.W. dept., Br. Guiana, 1882; 3rd cls. clk., G.P.O., 1893; 2nd cls. clk., audit dept., 1900; postmr.-gen., Br. Cent. Africa Prot., Jan., 1905.

FARRER, ROLAND J.—Ed. at Eton, and Balliol Coll., Oxon.; cadet, S. Sttlmts., Nov., 1896; ag. dist. offr., Nibong Tebal, Mar., 1897, to Sep., 1898, Dec., 1898, to Mar., 1900; ag. collr. land rev., Penang, Mar., 1900; ag dist. offr., Dindings, May, 1900; ag. supt. educ., Penang, June to Aug., 1900; head of Malay Coll., Malacca, May, 1901; ag. 2nd astt. col. sec., June, 1901; ag. dist. offr., Bukit Mertajam, May, 1902; confirmed, July, 1904; ag. dep. pub. proser., July, 1904; resumed duty as dist. offr., B. Mertajam, Feb., 1905.

FAULKNER, E.—Ed. at the gram. schl., Freestown; brigade office clk., S. Leone, 1876 to 1883; ch. clk. col. secretariat, 1883; astt. col. sec., 1889.

FAURE, HON. SIR P. H., K.C.M.G. (1898).—B. 1848; sec. for native affairs, Cape, July, 1890; col. sec., May, 1893; sec. for agricult., Jan., 1896, to Oct., 1898; col. sec., 1902-04; M.L.A. for Namaqualand, 1904.

FAWCETT, WILLIAM, B.Sc. (LOND.), F.L.S.—Asst. botanical dept., Br. Museum, 1880; dir. pub. gardens and plantations, Jamaica, 1886; mem. bd. of govs., Jamaica institute, 1887.

FAWKES, ARCHIBALD WALTER, K.C.—Ed. Repton schl.; B.A., St. John's Coll., Camb.; called
to bar, Inner Temp., Jan., 1879; registr., sup. ct., comsrr. of ct. of requests and of stamps, Malacca, 1884; ag. registr., sup. ct., Penang, 1885; pol. mag. and coroner, Gibraltar, 1886; acted as atty.-gen., 1890 and 1891; atty.-gen., Gibraltar, 1892; puisne judge, O.R.C., 1901.

FELDEN, Capt. R. B.—Capt., R.A.; ed. Wellington Coll.; lieut. R.A., July, 1884; A.D.C. and priv. sec. to gov., Barbados, May, 1890; to high comsrr., Cyprus, 1892; and to gov., Br. Guiana, 1898.

FELL, T. E., B.A., Cantab., 1897—Apptd. ch. clk., col. sec.'s off., G. Coast, 2nd Oct., 1897; ag. astt. col. sec., 14th Sep., 1899; inspr., preventive services, 4th Dec., 1899; ag. trav. comsrr., 1900-1901; trav. comsrr., 16th June, 1902; ag. comsrr. for nat. affairs, 26th June, 1902.

FERGUSON, DONALD.—Elected to provincial legislature, Pr. Ed. Is., 1878; apptd. to provl. cabinet in 1879, with the portfolio of pub. wks.; resig. the latter office in 1880, when he was apptd. provl. sec. and comsrr. of pub. lands; served as deleg. to Downing st. in 1886, regarding communication between P. E. Is. and mainland.

FERGUSSON, CLAUD.—Served during S. African war in I.Y. (King's and Queen's medals and clasps, D.C.M.); asst. sec., repatriation comsrr., Philippolis, Aug., 1902; sec., repat. coman., Bethulie, July, 1903; admstr., govt. relief dept., Senekal, Nov., 1903; inspr. of accts., govt. relief dept., O.R.C., May, 1904; astt. acctnt., educn. dept., O.R.C., Sept., 1904; ag. acctnt., ditto, 23rd June to 31st Oct., 1906.

FERGUSSON, RIGHT HON. SR JAMES, BART., P.C., M.P., G.C.S.I. (1885), K.C.M.G. (1874), C.I.E. (1880).—B. 1832; ed. at Rugby and Univ. Coll., Oxford; was lieut. and capt. of the Grenadier Guards; served in the Crimean campaign, including the battles of Alma and Inkerman (wounded) and siege of Sebastopol; was M.P. for Ayrshire, 1854-57 and 1859-68; unsuccessfully contested Sandwich, 1859, Frome, 1875, Greenock, 1878; was under-sec. of state for India and the home depts. in Lord Derby's 3rd, and Mr. Disraeli's 1st admstns.; gov. S. Australia, 1868; and gov. of N. Zealand, 1873; resig. 1874; gov. of Bombay, Mar., 1880, to Mar., 1885; M.P. for Manchester, 1885 and 1886; under-sec. of state foreign affairs 3rd Aug., 1886; postm. gen., 1891-92; d. 1907.

FERNANDEZ, HENRY.—Clerical astt. treas., Br. Guiana, 1887; 5th class clk., 1889; 4th class, 1891.

FERNANDO, MARCUS H.—Ed. Royal Coll., Colombo, and Univ. Coll., Lond.; Ceylon Govt. Univ. and Gilchrist scholar, 1883; B.Sc., 1886; M.B., 1888; gold medallist in med. and forensic med.; M.D., 1889; fellow of Univ. Coll., Lond., 1890; col. surg., civil med. dept., Ceylon; registr. of Ceylon Med. Coll., lecturer on pathology, 1890, and analyst to govt. of Ceylon; reported on epidemics of malarial fever, 1895; also in Bombay, 1897, on epidemics of plague; physician, gen. hosp., Colombo, 1897.

FRERREIRA, P. J., C.M.G. (1880).—Was comdt. of local cavalry in the Transvaal against Sikukuni.

FFOLIOTT, Lieut.-Col. O. HUMAN. Served in Imp. army, 1858-81; mil. sec. col. forces, Cape, June, 1882.

FFRENCH-MULLEN, VINCENT, L.R.C.S.I.—Dist. med. offr., Port Maria, Jamaica, Apr., 1881.

FIDDIES, GEORGE VANDELEUR, C.B. (1901), C.M.G. (1905), B.A.—B. 1858; ed. at Dulwich Coll. and late scholar of Brasenose Coll., Oxford; 2nd class mods., 1879; apptd., after compet., be a clk. in the office of the sec. of state for the cols., 25th Mar., 1881; priv. sec. to Earl of Onslow, Feb., 1887; and to Baron H. de Worms (afterwards Lord Pirbright), Feb., 1888, to Aug., 1892; priv. sec. to Sir R. Meade, 11th Mar., 1896; 1st class clk., 1896; imperial sec. and acctnt., to Sir A. Milner, high comsrr. for S. Africa, Sept., 1897; political sec. to Lord Roberts at Pretoria, June, 1900; sec. to the Transvaal administration, Dec., 1900; returned to C. O., 1902, as prin. clk.

FIDDIAN, ALEXANDER.—Ed. Univ. Coll., Cardiff, and Oxford; schlr. Pembroke Coll., 1893; 1st class classical honours, 1895; Goldsmiths co. exhibt., 1895; 1st class lit. hum., 1897; B.A., 1897; apptd., after compet. exam., 2nd class clk., C.O., Oct. 12th, 1897; astt. priv. sec. to Rt. Hon. Alfred Lyttelton, S. of S. for the colonies, 1st Apl., 1905.

FIELDING, HON. WILLIAM STEVENS.—Mem. for Halifax, Nova Scotia assem., 1882; declined premiership, but entered govt. without office in that year, and continued in that position till May, 1884, when he resig.; premier, provincial sec., and treas., Aug., 1884; min. of finance in Sir W. Laurier's admstn., June, 1896.

FINDLAY, HON. J. G., LL.D.—Atty.-gen. and col. sec., New Zealand.

FIRMSTONE, H. W.—Ed. at Rugby and Hertford Coll., Oxon (scholar); cadet, S. Sttlmts., 1890; passed final exam. in Chinese, Dec., 1893; ag. dist. offr., South Malacca, May, 1894; ag. astt. prot. of Chinese, Singapore, Jan., 1896; dist. offr. P.W., Oct., 1896; astt. protec. Chinese, Singapore, Feb., 1897; ag. astt. protec. Chinese, supt. Indian imgrts., and mun. comsrr. for Penang, Aug., 1898, to Feb., 1902, and from Aug., 1902; ag. prot. of Chinese, S.S., Feb. to July, 1902; ag. astt. ditto, Penang, Aug., 1902, to Feb., 1903, and from Aug., 1903; collr. of land rev. and offr. in charge of treas., Malacca, Jan., 1905.
